Round scope: the change since A2.4 splits the stage template into WhatIf_<env> (hosted ubuntu-latest, no environment) and Deploy_<env> (dependsOn WhatIf_<env>, no condition, self-hosted vnet pool, the only stage on policies-<env>). check-pipeline.py now asserts the stage structure. I read stage-template.yml and azure-pipelines.yml at HEAD. I did not diff the earlier checker.

Approval bypass: Deploy_<env> carries no stage condition, so the default succeeded() applies. A failed or skipped WhatIf_<env> skips Deploy_<env>. For prod, WhatIf_prod dependsOn Deploy_test, so a failure upstream skips it, then Deploy_prod. The gate.pipeline-schema receipt says mutant M2 (condition: always() on Deploy_<env>) fails the checker. The approval check is not in the repo. The template comment and QA step 32 state it must sit on the policies-<env> environment only.

S1 from A2.4 (the unapproved stage uses the subscription-scope ARM connection) is not re-raised. David rejected a separate what-if connection (inv-002 recommendation 3). The template records it as an accepted residual risk (stage-template.yml lines 19-21). It stays a P2 hardening note, not a finding. Limits on it: the pipeline triggers only on main with pr: none, and the stage runs az deployment sub what-if, which creates no deployment. It reads the drop artifact built in the same run, so the approver sees what Deploy applies.

What the layout adds: WhatIf_<env> reads the policies-<env> variable group before approval. That group holds only sqlAdminGroupObjectId, an Entra group object id and not a secret. Line 21 of the template states it must stay secret-free, which closes the A2.4 note. WhatIf_<env> uses no SQL service connection and no self-hosted pool, so it cannot reach the private SQL endpoint or the db_owner principal. Those stay in the approved Deploy stage.

The comment at stage-template.yml lines 17-18 warns that an approval check on the ARM service connection or the variable group would gate WhatIf_<env> and bring the QA defect back. That is a documented configuration constraint, not a code defect. It can't be checked offline.

API8: no secrets, connection strings with credentials or @secure parameters in infrastructure/. The grep hits are comments stating an absence plus the checker's own secret-scan regex. SQL is Entra-only, the app uses a managed identity with no password, and SQL has no public endpoint. App Insights is passed as an app setting, and its connection string is an ingestion endpoint, not a credential.
